text:
This looks like late 2016. The unemployment rate is 4.9%, the fed funds rate is about 0.37%, and the 10-year yield is 1.83%, which suggests roughly November 2016 or earlier. Core CPI at 2.34% fits the same period.

The 10-year yield fell 0.44 over the past 3 months, so it was higher 3 months earlier. That rules out November 2016, when yields jumped, and points to a date around February or March 2016 instead. Fed funds at 0.37% fits February 2016 (0.38%) or March 2016 (0.36%).

The 10-year yield was 2.24% in December 2015 and about 1.78% in February 2016. A 3-month change of -0.44 from 2.27% in November 2015 gives roughly 1.83%, which matches February 2016 at about 1.78% or March 2016 at about 1.89%. February's average was 1.78%, while the end-of-month value was about 1.74%. March's end value was 1.78%, so this is ambiguous.

The market data points to March 2016:
- US equity returned +4.3% over 1 month, while February was about flat, so March fits better.
- Emerging-market equity returned +9.1% over 1 month, which fits March 2016.
- Gold returned +15.1% over 3 months, which fits the January–March 2016 rally.
- Headline CPI at 0.97% year over year fits February 2016 (1.0%).
- Unemployment at 4.9% fits both months.
- The 12-month dollar change is -9.93, which is odd, but the 3-month change in the dollar's YoY rate is plausible.

I pick March 2016.
